userStories.title: Multi-pass spec generation pipeline with PM, Spec Writer, and UX Designer agents
userStories.description: Implement the first three passes of the six-pass spec generation pipeline. Pass 1 (PM Agent) converts brief to high-level spec with 10-20 coarse stories. Pass 2 (Spec Writer Agent) decomposes each story into exhaustive micro-stories covering every edge case, state, and interaction. Pass 3 (UX Designer Agent) adds explicit visual descriptions for every UI element, state, animation, and interaction pattern. Each pass creates a versioned spec in spec_versions table. Store pass metadata (which agent, timestamp, changes made) in spec JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/generate accepts optional 'passes' array parameter defaulting to ['pm', 'spec-writer', 'ux-designer']
Pass 1 (PM) generates 10-20 coarse stories from brief using direction stack context

Pass 2 (Spec Writer) decomposes each story into 3-10 atomic micro-stories with exhaustive granularity (e.g. 'add auth' becomes 15 tasks: schema, middleware, login route, token refresh, password reset, email verification, rate limiting, session management, logout, CSRF, validation, error messages, success states, loading states, empty states)

Pass 3 (UX Designer) adds visual descriptions to every story: button labels, field names, placeholders, layout positions, loading spinners, empty state copy, error message text, success confirmation copy, animations, transitions, focus states, hover states, disabled states
Each pass writes a spec_versions row with pass metadata JSON { passNumber, agentType, storiesAdded, storiesModified, timestamp }
Final spec JSON includes 'passes' array with metadata for each completed pass
Forge panel shows progress through passes with visual timeline (pass name + status badge + timestamp)
Each pass runs sequentially using chatComplete with agent-specific system prompts loaded from .rorca/personas/_review/ files

userStories.title: Best Practices, Adversarial Review, and Verifier agents (passes 4-6)
userStories.description: Implement the final three passes of the spec generation pipeline. Pass 4 (Best Practices Agent) annotates each story with library/framework convention guidance extracted from convention packs or CLAUDE.md. Pass 5 (Adversarial Review) runs Assumption Buster and Devil's Advocate personas to challenge the spec for contradictions, missing edge cases, and implicit assumptions. Pass 6 (Spec Verifier) performs final consistency checks: acceptance criteria are testable, no circular dependencies, every dependsOn target exists, no orphaned stories.
acceptanceCriteria: Pass 4 (Best Practices) reads convention pack or CLAUDE.md and adds convention annotations to each story (e.g. 'Use Tailwind space-y-4 not manual margin', 'Use shadcn/ui Button not raw <button>', 'Use Zod for validation schemas')

Pass 5 (Adversarial) runs two sub-agents: Assumption Buster (challenges implicit assumptions) and Devil's Advocate (argues against proposed approaches), aggregates feedback into story annotations and spec-level warnings array

Pass 6 (Verifier) validates: acceptance criteria use testable verbs (shows/hides/returns/emits not 'handles/supports'), dependsOn graph is acyclic, all dependsOn targets exist, no stories are unreachable from roots, story IDs are sequential
Adversarial warnings are stored in spec JSON 'warnings' array with { storyId, severity: 'info'|'warning'|'blocking', message, suggestedFix }
Forge panel shows warnings in expandable section above story list with severity badges and 'Apply Fix' button per warning
Spec Verifier blocks spec approval if any 'blocking' severity warnings exist
All three passes write spec_versions rows with pass metadata

userStories.title: Agent persona system with Primary, Adversarial, Specialist, and Review categories
userStories.description: Create the .rorca/personas/ directory structure with four subdirectories (_primary/, _adversarial/, _specialist/, _review/). Implement persona file loading and injection into execution engine buildPrompt(). Each persona is a markdown file with system prompt instructions, behavioral rules, and domain expertise. Personas attach to stories via 'persona' field (implementation agent) and 'reviewers' array (post-implementation review agents). Add GET/POST /api/personas routes for CRUD operations.
acceptanceCriteria: .rorca/personas/ directory created on 'rorca init' with subdirs _primary/, _adversarial/, _specialist/, _review/

Default personas shipped: architect.md, pm.md, lead-dev.md (primary), red-team.md, assumption-buster.md, devils-advocate.md (adversarial), frontend.md, backend.md, database.md, security.md, sre.md, ux-designer.md, qa.md (specialist), spec-writer.md, spec-verifier.md, best-practices.md (review)
buildPrompt() in execution-engine.ts reads persona file from .rorca/personas/<category>/<name>.md and injects as context layer after direction stack but before story prompt
Spec JSON stories support 'persona' string field and 'reviewers' string array field (persona names without .md extension)
GET /api/personas returns list of available personas grouped by category with { name, category, path, description } metadata
POST /api/personas creates or updates persona file with validation (markdown only, max 5KB, required description header)
Forge panel story cards show persona badge (icon + name) and reviewer badges in footer
AgentsEditorSection component in WorkspaceSettingsPanel allows creating/editing persona files with Monaco editor

userStories.title: Post-implementation adversarial review pipeline with diff analysis
userStories.description: After a story implementation completes (story_passed event), automatically trigger adversarial review passes using personas from story's 'reviewers' array. Each reviewer runs as a fresh subprocess with access to git diff of the story's commit. Reviewers can flag blocking issues that prevent story from merging. Results aggregated in story_comments table and displayed in Run View story detail panel.
acceptanceCriteria: execution-engine.ts emits 'story_review_started' WAL event after story_passed containing { storyId, reviewers: string[], commitSha }
Review orchestrator spawns one subprocess per reviewer persona with git diff piped to stdin and persona file injected into prompt
Each reviewer subprocess outputs structured JSON { storyId, reviewer, severity: 'pass'|'warning'|'blocking', findings: [{line, file, message, suggestedFix}] }
Findings written to story_comments table with reviewer name, timestamp, and findings JSON payload
If any reviewer returns severity='blocking', story status reverts to 'failed' and run pauses with HITL blocked state
Run View story detail panel shows review findings in expandable accordion sections grouped by reviewer with severity badges
Review findings include file:line clickable links that open diff view highlighting the flagged code
Blocking findings show 'Override and Merge' button (admin only) that allows force-passing despite review failure

userStories.title: Forge panel redesign with multi-pass progress timeline and interactive warnings
userStories.description: Redesign Forge panel to visualize the six-pass spec generation pipeline. Replace single 'Generate' button with multi-step progress timeline showing pass name, status (pending/running/complete/failed), timestamp, and agent icon. Add expandable warnings section above story list displaying adversarial review warnings with severity badges, apply-fix buttons, and drill-down to affected stories. Add pass comparison view to see spec evolution across passes.
acceptanceCriteria: Forge panel header shows horizontal timeline with 6 steps: PM → Spec Writer → UX Designer → Best Practices → Adversarial → Verifier
Each timeline step shows: agent icon (persona emoji or initial), step name, status badge (⏳ pending / 🔄 running / ✅ complete / ❌ failed), timestamp (if completed)
Active pass pulses with animated border and shows live token count and elapsed time
Warnings section appears between timeline and story list with collapsible accordion showing { count } warnings ({ blocking } blocking)

Each warning card shows: severity badge (🔵 info / 🟡 warning / 🔴 blocking), affected story title (clickable link), message, reviewer name, suggested fix (if available), 'Apply Fix' button (if fix available), 'Dismiss' button
Pass comparison view (new tab) shows side-by-side diff of spec JSON across passes with story additions/modifications/deletions highlighted
Brief input textarea moved to top with helper text: 'Describe what you want to build. Be specific about requirements, constraints, and success criteria.'
Generate button replaced with 'Start 6-Pass Generation' primary button that triggers POST /api/specs/generate with passes=['pm','spec-writer','ux-designer','best-practices','adversarial','verifier']

userStories.title: Story detail panel with exhaustive visual descriptions and accessibility audit
userStories.description: Add expandable story detail panel in Forge and Run View that shows all UX Designer visual descriptions, Best Practices annotations, and automated accessibility audit results. Each story displays: title, description, acceptance criteria, visual descriptions (button labels, field names, layout, states), convention annotations, WCAG compliance checklist, keyboard navigation flow diagram, screen reader experience description.
acceptanceCriteria: Story cards in Forge and Run View have 'View Details' button that opens slide-over panel

Detail panel sections: Overview (title/description/persona), Acceptance Criteria (expandable checklist), Visual Descriptions (from Pass 3 UX Designer), Convention Annotations (from Pass 4 Best Practices), Accessibility Audit (WCAG AA compliance checklist with pass/fail badges)

Visual Descriptions section shows structured fields: Button Labels (list with label + action), Form Fields (label + placeholder + validation + error messages), Loading States (spinner type + message + skeleton layout), Empty States (illustration + heading + body + CTA), Error States (icon + heading + message + retry button), Success States (confirmation message + next action)
Convention Annotations section shows library-specific guidance with code examples (e.g. 'Use shadcn/ui Button: <Button variant="default" size="sm">Label</Button>')

Accessibility Audit section shows WCAG 2.1 AA checklist: Color Contrast (4.5:1 minimum), Keyboard Navigation (tab order + focus indicators), ARIA Labels (all interactive elements labeled), Touch Targets (44px minimum), Screen Reader Experience (semantic HTML + live regions)
Keyboard navigation flow diagram (Mermaid flowchart) shows tab order through interactive elements with focus state descriptions
Screen reader experience description (prose) walks through how VoiceOver/NVDA would announce each element and state transition
Detail panel footer shows 'Edit Story' button (opens inline editor) and 'Run Story Solo' button (triggers pipeline with --story <ID> flag)

userStories.title: Accessibility-first UI components library with WCAG AA compliance
userStories.description: Create a shared components library in src/components/a11y/ with pre-built accessible primitives: Button, Input, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Dialog, Popover, Toast, Tabs, Accordion, Tooltip. Every component meets WCAG 2.1 AA standards: 4.5:1 contrast ratio, keyboard navigation, focus indicators, ARIA labels, screen reader announcements. Components use Radix UI primitives under the hood for behavior, Tailwind for styling.
acceptanceCriteria: src/components/a11y/ directory created with index.ts barrel export

Button component: supports variant (primary/secondary/ghost/danger), size (sm/md/lg), loading state (shows spinner + disables), disabled state (reduced opacity + cursor-not-allowed), keyboard focus (2px blue ring offset 2px), aria-label prop, aria-busy when loading

Input component: supports type (text/email/password/number), label (visually hidden or visible), placeholder, error state (red border + error icon + aria-describedby linking to error message), success state (green border + check icon), disabled state, required indicator (*), character count (live region announcing remaining chars)

Select component: native <select> for mobile, Radix Select for desktop, keyboard navigation (arrow keys + type-ahead), aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant, clear button (X icon, only when value selected)

Dialog component: Radix Dialog, focus trap, Esc to close, click outside to close (opt-in), aria-modal, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, initial focus on primary action, return focus to trigger on close
Toast component: auto-dismiss (configurable timeout), dismiss button (X icon), aria-live=polite for info, aria-live=assertive for errors, pause on hover, keyboard focus moves to toast when shown
All components export compound components (e.g. Accordion.Root/Item/Trigger/Content) following Radix naming conventions
Storybook stories for each component showing all states and keyboard interactions
Accessibility audit script (npm run a11y-audit) runs axe-core against Storybook and fails CI if violations found

userStories.title: Redesign all panels with new a11y component library and WCAG AA compliance audit
userStories.description: Refactor all 22 panels (Hub, Forge, Pipeline, Settings, Analytics, etc.) to use the new a11y component library from US-007. Replace all raw <button>, <input>, <select> with accessible primitives. Add keyboard shortcuts panel (⌘K), skip-to-content links, focus management on route changes, high contrast mode toggle, reduced motion mode (respects prefers-reduced-motion). Run automated axe-core audit on all panels and fix violations.
acceptanceCriteria: All panels import components from src/components/a11y/ instead of raw HTML elements
Keyboard shortcuts panel (⌘K) shows searchable list of all shortcuts with OS-specific modifier keys (⌘ on Mac, Ctrl on Windows/Linux)
Skip-to-content link appears at top of every panel (visually hidden until focused, jumps to main content region on click)
Route changes announce page title to screen readers via aria-live region and move focus to <h1> heading
High contrast mode toggle in Settings > Accessibility increases all contrast ratios to 7:1 (WCAG AAA) and disables subtle shadows/gradients
Reduced motion mode (auto-detected from prefers-reduced-motion or manually toggled) disables all animations, transitions, and auto-playing content
All interactive elements have visible focus indicators (2px blue ring offset 2px) and :focus-visible styling (no ring on mouse click, ring on keyboard focus)
All form inputs have associated <label> elements (explicit for attribute or wrapping), all images have alt text, all icons have aria-label
Automated axe-core audit (npm run a11y-audit) runs against all 22 panels in headless browser and fails if any violations found

Accessibility audit results displayed in new Settings > Accessibility > Audit tab showing violations grouped by severity (critical/serious/moderate/minor) with file:line links and remediation guidance
